4
The output of a signal generator is connected to a cathode-ray oscilloscope (CRO). A trace is
shown on the screen.
1.0 cm
1.0 cm
The time-base of the CRO is set at 2.00 ms cm–1.
What is the frequency of the signal?
A
50 Hz
B
125 Hz
C
250 Hz
D
500 Hz

hints: Count the horizontal length of one complete sine wave on the screen using the $1.0\text{ cm}$ grid - look from one peak to the next peak.
Multiply that length in $\text{cm}$ by the time-base $2.00\text{ ms cm}^{-1}$ to get the period $T$ in $\text{ms}$.
Use $f = 1/T$ with $T$ converted to seconds to find the frequency in $\text{Hz}$.
walkthrough: Measure one full cycle from the CRO trace. From peak to peak the wave repeats every $4.0\text{ cm}$ using the $1.0\text{ cm}$ squares.
The time-base tells the time for each centimetre horizontally: $2.00\text{ ms cm}^{-1}$.

A.explanation: A frequency of $50\text{ Hz}$ means $T = 20\text{ ms}$, which would need $10\text{ cm}$ for one cycle at $2.00\text{ ms cm}^{-1}$, much longer than shown.

B.explanation: One cycle is $4.0\text{ cm}$, so $T = 8.00\text{ ms}$ and $f = 1/T = 125\text{ Hz}$.

C.explanation: A frequency of $250\text{ Hz}$ means $T = 4.0\text{ ms}$ or $2.0\text{ cm}$, which is only half the observed full sine-wave cycle.

D.explanation: A frequency of $500\text{ Hz}$ means $T = 2.0\text{ ms}$ or $1.0\text{ cm}$, which confuses one grid square with one full period.
